messages:
Kenji Nakamura: Posting for copy + warning-state review on the Hosted Canary Rollout wizard. Figma here: https://figma.com/file/RWDX-CanaryWizard?node-id=742%3A1889

Kenji Nakamura: Main things I need eyes on:
1) “Risk” warning on Schedule step (traffic split)
2) Confirmation modals (Start rollout / Advance step / Roll back)
3) Error states: policy denial (approval required), soak-time violation, and auto-pause due to SLO breach

Kenji Nakamura: I dropped draft copy in the components as text styles. Reply here w/ edits pls.

Tessa Morgan: :eyes: taking a look now. first impression: too much scary language on the schedule screen. we should be precise about what can happen + what protections exist.

Marissa Cole: +1. We got feedback from beta invite calls that “canary” already feels risky. We should frame as “safety rails” not “you’re about to break prod.”

Nora Ahmed: Looking specifically at warning banners + empty/error states. Some of these read like internal errors, not customer-actionable.

Dylan Brooks: Eng POV: we should avoid copy that implies we guarantee rollback will fix everything. Auto-rollback is best-effort + depends on policy settings.

Kenji Nakamura: Ok. Here’s the current banner copy on Schedule step:
“Warning: Canary rollouts can cause increased error rates, latency, or degraded quality. Proceed only if you can monitor metrics and rollback quickly.”

Tessa Morgan: Suggest:
Title: “Monitor baseline vs canary metrics during rollout”
Body: “Traffic will be split between baseline and canary. Set stop conditions and review cohort metrics between steps. You can pause or roll back at any time.”

Marissa Cole: Can we also add a single-line callout about step changes being auditable / approval gates? For enterprise folks it’s a comfort signal.

Kenji Nakamura: That’s good. Maybe: “All rollout actions are recorded in Activity.”

Felix Schneider: On metrics view we already have “Baseline vs canary” compare. For wizard banner we can link: “View cohort metrics” or “Learn more.”

Nora Ahmed: +1 to a link. Banner should not try to teach everything. I’d avoid “degraded quality” unless we actually have quality metrics wired. For GA it’s optional/manual.

Dylan Brooks: Agree. “degraded quality” will raise expectations that we detect it automatically.

Kenji Nakamura: So remove explicit “quality” from warning?

Marissa Cole: I’d say keep it generic but accurate. Like “behavior changes” not “quality.”

Tessa Morgan: +1. “Output may change” covers it without promising detection.

Kenji Nakamura: Proposed banner v2:
Title: “Monitor changes during rollout”
Body: “Traffic will be split between baseline and canary. Review cohort metrics between steps. You can pause or roll back at any time. All rollout actions are recorded in Activity.”

Felix Schneider: Works. Might tweak “recorded” -> “logged” for consistency with Audit Log language.

Jordan Lee: jumping in from policy side — we should avoid “at any time” if approvals are required. For some tenants, rollback requires approver. Same for advancing steps.

Kenji Nakamura: Good catch. So: “You can request a pause or rollback at any time”??

Marissa Cole: Maybe: “You can pause at any time. Rollback may require approval depending on your policy.”

Tessa Morgan: that’s getting long again. Alternative: “Actions are subject to your rollout policy.” + link “View policy”.

Jordan Lee: “subject to policy” is accurate + short.

Kenji Nakamura: Updated banner:
Title: “Monitor changes during rollout”
Body: “Traffic will be split between baseline and canary. Review cohort metrics between steps. Actions are subject to your rollout policy. All rollout actions are logged.”

Nora Ahmed: :thumbsup: Also can we add a subtle link style “View policy” that opens the side panel? (if we have it)

Dylan Brooks: We have policy details on Review step via the preview endpoint (max step size, min soak, approval required). We can surface it in a drawer.

Kenji Nakamura: Cool, I’ll add “View rollout policy” link in the banner.

Kenji Nakamura: Next: destructive confirmation modals.
Current “Rollback” modal title: “Roll back rollout?”
Body: “This will immediately send 100% of traffic to the baseline. Canary traffic will be set to 0%.”
Primary button: “Roll back” (red)

Tessa Morgan: Pretty good. Add consequences + non-reversible note? But rollback is reversible (you can start a new rollout). Don’t say irreversible.

Nora Ahmed: Consider adding “This may take up to X minutes to fully apply across regions” (if true). People will otherwise panic when they still see some canary requests.

Dylan Brooks: Propagation isn’t instant, but should be fast (<60s typically). We can say “may take a few minutes.”

Felix Schneider: Metrics lag too. We should avoid “immediately” in the modal.

Kenji Nakamura: Great point. Replace “immediately” with “as the change propagates”.

Marissa Cole: Also, rollback might still be blocked by approval gate. In that case they won’t see this confirm modal? Or they will and then get denied?

Jordan Lee: Ideally Console does a preflight. If approval required, “Request rollback” flow instead of “Roll back now.” (Policy returns `requires_approval`.)

Kenji Nakamura: I have two variants mocked:
A) Confirm rollback (if permitted)
B) “Approval required” modal (if not)

Tessa Morgan: Let’s review B. What’s the copy?

Kenji Nakamura: Title: “Approval required”
Body: “Your organization requires approval to roll back a rollout. Request approval from a rollout approver.”
CTA: “Request approval”
Secondary: “Cancel”

Tessa Morgan: That’s fine. Add hint on where request goes (Activity + notifications). Otherwise users wonder if anything happened.

Nora Ahmed: +1. “A request will be added to Activity and visible to approvers.”

Jordan Lee: Also include who counts as approver? We can show role name “Rollout Approver” at least.

Kenji Nakamura: ok: “Request will appear in Activity for users with the Rollout Approver role.”

Marissa Cole: Love that.

Wei Chen: (docs) Noted: make sure “Rollout Approver” matches docs terminology. We’ve been using “rollout-approver” internally; customer facing should be “Rollout approver”.

Svetlana Orlov: From design systems: confirm modals should follow DS pattern:
- Title case
- Body max 2 lines before “Learn more”
- Primary button verb first (“Request approval”, “Advance step”, etc)

Kenji Nakamura: good call. I’ll trim.

Kenji Nakamura: Advance-step modal copy currently:
Title: “Advance to 25%?”
Body: “This will increase canary traffic from 5% to 25%. Stop conditions remain active.”

Tessa Morgan: “Stop conditions remain active” is great reassurance.

Dylan Brooks: Add “Minimum soak time: 30m” if policy enforces. If they try early, we should show a blocking error state not this modal.

Nora Ahmed: Yes. If early, error should be actionable: “Try again in 12m” + “Override requires approval” (if that’s a thing).

Jordan Lee: For GA, no override unless explicitly allowed by policy (rare). Default is deny. Message should be deterministic.

Kenji Nakamura: Ok, onto error states.

Kenji Nakamura: Soak-time violation state (when user clicks Advance):
Current inline error banner: “You can’t advance yet. Minimum soak time has not elapsed.”

Nora Ahmed: Change to:
Title: “Soak time not met”
Body: “This step requires at least 30 minutes of soak time. Try again in 12 minutes.”
Link: “View policy”

Tessa Morgan: +1. Also we should avoid “can’t” / “not allowed” tone. More neutral.

Marissa Cole: This is the one that will create a lot of tickets if unclear. Add a line: “This helps catch regressions before increasing traffic.”

Felix Schneider: careful adding educational text inside error. maybe as tooltip.

Kenji Nakamura: Maybe keep the error concise; add helper text under the timeline: “Soak time helps catch regressions before increasing traffic.”

Tessa Morgan: that works.

Kenji Nakamura: Policy denial (step size too large) current:
“Denied by policy: max step increase is 20%.”

Jordan Lee: Please don’t say “Denied by policy” (sounds like internal). Suggest:
“Step change exceeds your rollout policy”
Details: “Max allowed increase is 20%. Update the next step or edit policy.” (If edit policy is allowed)

Marissa Cole: Editing policy probably admin-only; we can say “Contact an admin to change policy.”

Kenji Nakamura: ok.

Nora Ahmed: Also we need a “learn why” link. People will ask “why 20%?” but that’s org policy.

Wei Chen: For docs, we should align phrasing to “rollout policy guardrails.” If UI says “rollout policy” and docs say “guardrails” that’s okay as long as we explain they’re the same.

Kenji Nakamura: last one: Auto-pause due to SLO breach.
Current toast copy: “Rollout paused. Stop condition triggered.”
Timeline row: “Auto-paused: p95 latency exceeded threshold.”

Tessa Morgan: Toast is too vague. Toast should include the specific signal.

Felix Schneider: Agree. “Paused: p95 latency +35% vs baseline (threshold 20%)” if we have the numbers.

Dylan Brooks: We have data from evaluator but sometimes missing if metrics query times out. We should handle both:
- with metrics: show values
- without: “Paused due to stop condition. View details.”

Nora Ahmed: Great. And the details panel should show:
- what triggered
- time window
- recommended action buttons: “Rollback” / “Resume” (if allowed) / “Acknowledge”

Marissa Cole: Also ensure we don’t imply it’s a platform outage. It’s a safety action.

Kenji Nakamura: I’ll update:
Toast: “Paused: p95 latency stop condition triggered”
Subtext: “View details in Activity”

Tessa Morgan: Make it “Activity” or “Timeline”? In mocks it’s “Activity” panel.

Kenji Nakamura: It’s labeled “Activity” in the right rail, “Timeline” in the main panel. I’ll standardize to “Activity”.

Svetlana Orlov: +1 on consistency. DS wise, use same term for nav + headers.

Kenji Nakamura: Action items I’m taking:
- Replace schedule warning with shorter “Monitor changes during rollout” banner + “View rollout policy” link; remove “degraded quality” language.
- Update rollback modal: remove “immediately”, add propagation note, add approval-required variant w/ “Request approval” and mention Rollout approver role.
- Update soak-time + max step size errors to be actionable (“Try again in X”, “Max allowed is Y”) + link to policy.
- Improve auto-pause toast to include signal where possible + fallback copy.

Marissa Cole: :thumbsup: Please also add a tiny line on Review step: “All actions are logged to Audit Log” (for enterprise reassurance). Not a banner, just helper text.

Wei Chen: If you can paste final strings in a doc or comment, I’ll mirror in the docs PR. Otherwise we’ll drift.

Kenji Nakamura: Will do. I’ll drop final copy in a comment on the Figma page + link it here once updated.

Dylan Brooks: cc me when done; I want to ensure the UI copy matches actual error codes we return (`requires_approval`, `min_soak_not_met`, `max_step_exceeded`, etc.).

Kenji Nakamura: yep. will ping.

Tessa Morgan: Thanks. This is close. Biggest win is making the warnings feel supportive, not scary.
